subject: Request: Verify 11/30 service gap and credit plan
messages:
From: Sarah Huang <sarah.huang@fintechco.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTech Co Support <support@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T15:22:00Z
Subject: Unplanned 503s during peak — please confirm downtime window and credit eligibility

Markus,

We observed a critical spike in 503/504 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoint (/v1/generate streaming) during our peak batch run this afternoon. Symptoms: stalled streaming responses, ~25% failure rate for the batch job, and heartbeats showing retries from our side. The timeframe we captured in our CI logs is 2027-11-30T14:03:22Z -> 2027-11-30T15:12:47Z (UTC). Our telemetry shows a significant uptick in end-to-end latency just before the failures.

Can you confirm whether Redwood measured a service gap during that window and advise on credit eligibility per our SLA? We need an initial confirmation for procurement and finance before we open a formal claim. Also attaching our client-side ingestion trace (trace_20271130-14-00_to_15-30.log.gz) — please let us know if you need additional artifacts.

Thanks,
Sarah Huang
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTech Co

Attachments: trace_20271130-14-00_to_15-30.log.gz
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30T15:37:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Unplanned 503s during peak — FinTech Co asking for confirmation and credit eligibility

Team — forwarding FinTech Co's note. They sent a precise window and a client-side trace. Quick asks:
- Can SRE/opsgroup confirm whether the control plane or serving observed an availability gap covering 14:03–15:12 UTC?
- If confirmed, what’s the preliminary classification (partial degradation vs total unavailability) and whether it meets SLA credit thresholds (per our hosted SLA for enterprise customers)?
- Neha: please flag any regulatory/customer-data scope concerns — they included a trace; I preserved it in drive (ingestion-metrics-20271130.csv + trace).

Customer-facing: I want to give Sarah something within 24 hours — initial confirmation and an expected timeline for a postmortem/credit calculation.

Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: trace_20271130-14-00_to_15-30.log.gz, ingestion-metrics-20271130.csv
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unplanned 503s during peak — FinTech Co asking for confirmation and credit eligibility

Markus / team,

Quick initial findings from the incident timeline: our serving telemetry and ingest logs show a localized degradation in the US-east serving pool beginning at ~2027-11-30T14:02:50Z and resolving by ~2027-11-30T15:10:30Z. Impacted routes: streaming generation (/v1/generate) and the KV cache sync endpoint. There was a spike of internal retries and a transient load-shedding event on a subset of machines which correlated with a failed autoscaler decision during a short control-plane lag.

Classification: partial availability degradation affecting ~18% of global requests for that region and period. Per our SLA terms (hosted customers, monthly availability buckets), this looks like a degradational event that could be eligible for pro-rata credit depending on exact impacted request volume and configured SLOs.

Evidence attached: aggregated ingress/egress counters (ingestion-metrics-20271130.csv) and sampled serving traces. Next steps I recommend:
- SRE to extract exact per-customer request counts for FT-4821 within the window (I can run the query but need ops access to the billing counters).
- Postmortem: we should assign an owner (ops + runtime). I'll coordinate a 72-hour postmortem and include timeline, root cause, and remediation.
- Customer comms: initial confirmation to Sarah that we saw a degradation and that we are evaluating credit eligibility; offer a provisional pro-rata credit and follow up with exact calculation after we pull request-volume metrics.

Neha: I scanned the customer trace for PII — nothing sensitive in the snippet, but we should avoid storing raw traces outside approved storage. I'll host artifacts in the incident Drive link and share a redacted excerpt to the customer.

Evelyn
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ingestion-metrics-20271130.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Huang <sarah.huang@fintechco.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, FinTech Co Support <support@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Unplanned 503s during peak — initial confirmation and next steps

Sarah,

Thanks for the trace and for flagging this. We’ve confirmed there was a partial serving degradation affecting a subset of US-east instances between ~2027-11-30T14:02:50Z and ~2027-11-30T15:10:30Z UTC. Evelyn and the ops team are coordinating a postmortem; I’ve asked SRE to pull precise per-customer request volumes during the window so we can compute a pro-rata credit under your current SLA.

Preliminarily: this appears to meet our degradation threshold for a pro-rata credit (not a full-month credit). Expected timeline:
- Today: initial confirmation (this message) and redacted artifacts posted to our incident drive.
- 48–72 hours: complete postmortem with root cause and remediation plan.
- 5 business days: exact credit calculation and formal credit note (applied to your next invoice) unless you prefer an immediate provisional credit.

If you’d like a provisional credit now we can apply an interim pro-rata and reconcile after the exact numbers are calculated. Let me know which you prefer.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll include measures in the postmortem to prevent autoscaler/control-plane mismatch in similar load patterns.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/teams/ops/incident/2027-11-30/summary (redacted traces + metrics)
